environment.note: No language model was used at any point in this evaluation. Every decision is produced by deterministic rules, so the numbers are reproducible from the seed with no provider dependency.

arms.unguarded_passthrough: No gateway. Every proposed tool call is forwarded. Establishes the benign completion ceiling and the zero-protection floor.
arms.keyword_classifier: Blocks a call when the tool name or any argument string matches a list of dangerous keywords. No notion of a task, a scope, a budget or an approval.
arms.contract_policy: Agent Drift's deterministic policy engine evaluating each call against the approved intent contract for its task, with the same enforcement order and the same upstream input schemas the gateway applies.

target_checks.detail: policy evaluation only, excluding the upstream call

limitations: **A perfect or near-perfect score here does not mean the system is robust.** Cases are constructed by the authors of the policy, so the labels encode the same understanding of the contracts that the rules encode. What a high score demonstrates is internal consistency -- the rules do what their authors believe the contracts say -- plus the absence of the specific failure modes enumerated here. It is not evidence about attacks nobody thought to write down. Five families are held out to make overfitting visible, but a held-out family is still an author-chosen family.

Two defects in this project were found by running this suite rather than by reasoning: undeclared arguments such as `force: true` were being forwarded, and `docs/../docs/x` was being rejected as traversal when it is a legitimate spelling of `docs/x`. Both are fixed (see docs/DECISIONS.md D-013). That the suite found them is the argument for it; that it took a run to find them is the argument against trusting a score alone.
Decisions are deterministic, so repeated runs give identical outcomes. The only variance is in the latency measurement.

This suite measures argument-level authorization. It does not measure end-to-end agent task success, and it says nothing about harm that is only visible across a sequence of individually in-contract calls.
The keyword baseline is one reasonable implementation, not the best possible text classifier. It bounds what naive filtering achieves, not what filtering could achieve.
The unguarded arm has no latency cost by construction; its latency figures measure the harness, not a real system.
